findings.failure_scenario: An operator reading the help text expects 3 clears to be enough for a baseline or top-up goal and is surprised by the kills_per_batch refusal. The behavior is correct; only the wording is misleading.
findings.summary: Stale text after the kills_per_batch change: the set_baseline docstring (line 80) and --target-kills help (line 148) still say kills_per_measurement; the baseline_problems docstring and --force help still say 'counted non-clears'; the scoreboard_run.py line 264 comment still describes kills_per_measurement as the goal.

findings.failure_scenario: A target file with kills_per_batch set to 0 or null makes set_baseline and run fall back to kills_per_measurement while the keep rule uses 0 (or fails on null). No current target does this.
findings.summary: set_baseline and scoreboard_run.py (lines 266 and 275) write out the batch-size rule again instead of calling scoreboard_core.kills_per_batch(); the two differ only when kills_per_batch is 0 or null.

findings.failure_scenario: Every default `scoreboard show` against r3-47cd175 returns insufficient_kills because of the baseline-side batch shortfall until the label is topped up to 5 clears (the top-up goal now defaults to 5; its binary is required) or a new 5-clear baseline is set.
findings.summary: The committed baseline pointer r3-47cd175 has 4 counted clears, below the new kills_per_batch 5 minimum, and load_baseline does not recheck it. This is workflow state, not a code defect.

findings.failure_scenario: A deliberately forged transcript with the correct layout, meta file, cwd and sessionId still passes. A coordinator root containing '.' or '_' (for example a .claude/worktrees path) would reject a genuine transcript with transcript_identity_mismatch; this fails closed and does not affect the current root.
findings.summary: The transcript binding is now tied to the location, meta file, session and cwd, but it is not cryptographic (same as the Codex rollout path). _project_slug replaces only '/', while Claude Code replaces every non-alphanumeric character.
